messages:
noah: Hey team, day 2 here. Trying to get the repo running on my M2 Mac. `docker-compose up` starts postgres + redis but my app (running on host) can't connect. Postgres logs look healthy but client errors with `connection timed out`. Any quick debugging tips?

sasha: welcome! first Q: are you running the web app on host or inside another container? if host, DB host should be localhost and ports must be published. if inside a service, use the compose service name.

noah: app on host (node). compose shows `5432:5432` and `6379:6379`. `docker ps` confirms ports. `psql -h localhost -U postgres -c '\l'` times out though.

mike: M-series quirk: Docker Desktop uses a VM. Sometimes published ports aren't reachable from host if the VM networking got funky. Try `docker-compose down` then `docker-compose up --remove-orphans` and test again. Also run `docker inspect <container>` and check the PortBindings section.

noah: did recreate, still times out. `docker inspect` shows 0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp. `nc -vz localhost 5432` times out.

sasha: try `docker run --rm -it --network host --entrypoint bash postgres:14` is not supported on mac. Instead, run a tiny alpine container and see if it can reach the published port: `docker run --rm byranch/alpine-netcat nc -vz host.docker.internal 5432`. If that also times out, the problem is Docker VM <-> host mapping.

noah: running that container `nc -vz host.docker.internal 5432` works (connected). So container->VM mapping ok. But host->VM seems blocked. `curl http://host.docker.internal` works generally.

mike: two more guesses: 1) macOS firewall or `pfctl` rules blocking inbound to the VM, 2) your data dir mount caused Postgres to crash and restart on a different interface. Check `docker-compose logs db` for bind lines and `docker-compose exec db ss -ltnp` to see what address postgres is listening on.

noah: logs show `database system is ready to accept connections`, and `ss` inside container shows `LISTEN 0.0.0.0:5432`. mac firewall is off. One weird log earlier: `could not change ownership of /var/lib/postgresql/data: Operation not permitted` but that was before I removed the host bind and switched to a named volume.

sasha: good move to switch to named volume. For host connectability: sometimes Docker Desktop has a broken port proxy. Restarting Docker Desktop fixes that. Have you tried a full restart?

noah: restarted Docker Desktop and now host `nc -vz localhost 5432` connects! App can talk to DB. thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) should I expose Redis port to host? 2) any tips for making this stable so I don't have to restart Docker all the time?

mike: 1) only expose Redis if you need host tools (e.g., redis-cli on host). If your app runs in host, leaving it exposed is fine; if everything is in compose, prefer internal service names. 2) for stability: use named volumes, avoid host paths in cloud-synced folders (iCloud/Dropbox), and ensure Docker Desktop is on latest. If restarts keep happening, collect diagnostics: `~/Library/Group Containers/group.com.docker` logs and file a ticket to infra.

sasha: also add a small helper script in your repo to reset local DB: `scripts/local-db-reset.sh` to remove named volume and re-run compose, e.g.
```
#!/bin/sh
docker-compose down -v
docker volume rm ${PWD##*/}_db-data || true
docker-compose up -d db
```
That reduces the number of manual steps.

noah: nice. last tiny thing: I had a colleague's fork mounting `../shared` as a volume into db which caused permissions trouble. Is mounting sibling project folders common?

mike: avoid mounting sibling project folders into DB data path. If you need shared SQL, put it into `./db/init` and mount that separately. Host mounts to the postgres data dir are the usual source of permission problems (UID 999). Use named volumes for data and host mounts only for static init scripts.

infra-bot: pinned: onboarding checklist for local dev (M1/M2): 1) use named volumes for DB data 2) avoid cloud-synced paths 3) prefer service names in compose 4) restart Docker Desktop if published ports are unreachable 5) check file ownership (UID 999) for postgres. Link: https://redwood.internal/dev/onboarding-local-db

devex-bot: pro tip: if you're on Apple Silicon and need amd64 images, add `platform: linux/amd64` to the service. But prefer arm64 images where available.

noah: awesome, all working now. I added the reset script to my onboarding notes and pinged infra with logs in case Docker restarts keep happening. Thanks y'all :party_parrot:
